problem:
$\,$ $∀\,ϵ\in {R}^{+},\,∃\,x\in Q,\,-ϵ<x<ϵ.$

Which of the following expresses the statement given above?

choices.value: There exists a rational number $x$ such that for all $ϵ>0,$ $-ϵ<x<ϵ.$
Given any rational number $ϵ>0$ there exists a real number $x$ such that $-ϵ<x<ϵ.$
There exists a number $x$ such that for all $ϵ,$ $-ϵ<x<ϵ.$
There exists a positive real number $ϵ$ such that for all rational numbers $x,$ $-ϵ<x<ϵ.$
Given any real number $ϵ>0$ there exists a rational number $x$ such that $-ϵ<x<ϵ.$

feedback.problem:
$\,$ $∃\,n\in N,\,∀\,m\in Z,\,nm$ is divisible by $2.$

Which of the following expresses the statement given above?
feedback.worked_solution:
Our quantified statement reads as follows:

$\,$ **There exists** $n\in N$ **such that**, **for all** $m\in Z,\,nm$ is divisible by $2.$

This can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ There exists a natural number $n$ such that the product of $n$ and any integer $m$ is divisible by $2.$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: There exists a natural number $n$ such that the product of $n$ and any integer $m$ is divisible by $2.$
